summary: This rewrite stage only fixes faults, and the target is real: Marlin takes 254-443 us at verify_16/32 against a MoE floor of about 101-109 us. The fixes don't identify the 715 root cause, so treat this run as a diagnostic okc check whose main job is to name the faulting kernel. That only works if the logging is unbuffered and announces each launch before it starts.
justification: Mechanism is plausible. FINDINGS shows Marlin at 271.6/326.1 us (sliding/full verify_16) and 443.2/449.7 us (verify_32), 47-70% of layer time, running at about 1.1-1.2 TB/s against a weight-stream floor of roughly 101-109 us. A persistent 132-CTA swap-AB mma.sync kernel that streams each touched local expert once per chunk of up to 64 routes can reasonably reach about 2 TB/s on H100. The 'decode_* / verify_1 flat' controls are consistent because the tokens > 32 gate only admits T=128/256. Rewrite milestones M1-M3 can be read from profile top_kernels (moe_w13_silu_swapab plus moe_w2_swapab plus moe_route_list against Marlin x2 plus act_and_mul plus align). Weakest link: neither of the 'proven-form' swaps clearly removes the fault. (3) is probably a SASS no-op, because cuda_bf16.hpp implements __hmul2 for bf16 on sm_90 as fma.rn.bf16x2 with a -0.0 addend, i.e. the same instruction as before. (2) createpolicy/cache_hint is standard CUTLASS PTX on sm_80+ and an unlikely trap source. ptxas accepted every form, so an encoding problem is less likely than a trap inside a .sync.aligned collective (ldmatrix/mma inside `if (f < me_nf)`), a stray trap/assert, or a bad smem configuration. The run will probably fault again. Its value is the canary ladder that attributes the fault, which the sibling moe failure never got. -lineinfo will not name the instruction in a judge log without compute-sanitizer. Two design points check out: chunk capacity (routes//64 + 33 >= worst case sum ceil(c_e/64) <= routes/64 + 32), and the bf16 rounding of hg/hu before silu, which matches Marlin's bf16 w13 output.
confounders: stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1: at T>32 the new moe_route_list replaces master's parallel align on the side stream. The incumbent is therefore parallel-align + Marlin, which is the right baseline. Stream placement matters, though: the new kernels must run on state['side_stream'] inside the existing wait_stream fence (submission.py ~1830-1844). Otherwise a gain or loss may come partly from lost or gained overlap rather than from the GEMMs. Read kernel times, not the headline.

marlin-block-m-cap-16: the incumbent Marlin times (254-449 us) are measured with block_m capped at 16 at T=128/256. A different cap would move the incumbent, not this kernel. Comparing against today's master is correct and needs no A/B.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: gated to small T, so at T>32 the SGLang fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum consumes y. It is not a confounder, as long as y's layout ([T,8,K], remote rows never read, slot_expert_ids=local_ids) is unchanged.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite stage whose first measurement must be an okc check. Its main outcomes are 'faults with the kernel named' or 'passes, and the kernel times can be read against Marlin per shape', and a revert or tune of any landed item disambiguates neither. The decode_*/verify_1 shapes act as built-in controls because they fall outside the gate. If it passes, the next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: No child processes: confirmed as specified. Keep any self-check strictly in-process, with no multiprocessing or subprocess imports anywhere (okc_lint).

torch.cuda.synchronize(), the prints and the CUDA-event timing must stay in prepare() only. kernel_fn must stay graph-capturable: no .item(), and n_chunks is read on the device with a fixed grid of 132, as in the patch. Keep it that way.

Setting TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST via os.environ affects every later load_inline in the process (dense-chain TU). Prefer passing -gencode arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a in extra_cuda_cflags for this TU only, or set and restore the variable around this build. Watch the 300 s prepare budget: about 42 s per TU, plus the canaries and the T=40/128/256 self-check.
Precision: act and y stay bf16, dequant is exact, and accumulation is fp32. OK. The prefill_nan buffers are self-check only and must not appear in the timed path.
open_questions: Prints must use flush=True (or sys.stdout.flush()), and each kernel needs a 'launching <kernel>' line before its launch as well as an 'ok' line after its synchronize. A sticky 715 kills the worker, and buffered stdout would lose exactly the line that names the kernel.

Order the canaries so each step adds one suspect form: cvt e4m3x2 alone, then dequant8 (hmul2) alone, then ldmatrix.x4 plus one mma.sync tile, then cp.async.cg at the 221 KB smem configuration, then the route list, then w13, then w2. A fault then identifies a form, not just a kernel.

Is the __hmul2 change actually different SASS from the old fma.rn.bf16x2 with a -0 addend? If not, add a cuobjdump/SASS note to the attempt file so the next stage does not count it as an eliminated suspect.

If the canaries pass but the full launch faults, the remaining suspects are an unconverged .sync.aligned collective (me_nf or item-end not truly CTA-uniform across persistent items) and the 221 KB smem configuration. A next stage could test 2 stages and about 120 KB smem.
